The Get Ready strip's character set: 96 characters, one for each tile, its miniature drawn in four rows of two-pixel dots, to $A2FF. get_ready exchanges $A000-$A3FF with $6000-$63FF (memory_swap 3), raster_ready_strip points the VIC at a character set at $6000 ($D018 = $19) for the strip, and get_ready_strip writes each map byte there as a character; leaving the Get Ready screen the same swap puts sprite blocks $80-$8F back. So the swap also carries this file's $A300-$A3FF, the oxygen code, out to $6300 and back while the Get Ready screen shows.

One byte, 0, that nothing reads while world 2 is in memory. The label is the engine's: player_dead reads five water characters from $A300 on stages 1 and 2, and player_hit compares the frame that touched Clyde with $A300-$A304 from stage 6 on.

The frames to the oxygen bar's next step, counted down by oxygen_drain on each frame Clyde swims and reloaded with $3E, so a step every 63 frames; stage_main_setup writes $32 here when stages 4 to 6 start ($1AD4). A refill does not reset it.

Fills the OXYGEN bar under the panel's score: oxygen_fill_block draws oxygen_bar_rows into byte column 0-2 of sprite block 2 from row 13 ($40A7), then falls into oxygen_fill_block again for block 3 ($40E7). These are the panel sprites whose rows 0-7 hold the score's digits (score_draw); panel_lower shows their lower rows only while $1213 says Clyde swims. player_hit_world2 jumps here when Clyde touches a sprite showing frames $85-$88, the rising bubbles (type 41), and stage_main_setup calls it when stages 4 to 6 start. Nothing else fills it: coming up out of the water does not.

Draws the bar into one sprite block: the low byte of its first byte arrives in A and goes into the STA's operand (a_A319); three passes, one for each byte column, each copying oxygen_bar_rows' eight bytes into rows 13-20 (every third byte from the operand's address, X from $15 down by 3) and moving the operand on a column. Then the bar's state is full: $1253 (the step within a column) 0 and oxygen_column 6.
The low byte of the STA's operand at $A318 ($40A7 or $40E7 to start, then one more each pass); its high byte stays $40.
The operand of the LDX at $A324: the passes left (2, 1, 0), stored at $A30E and reloaded to count them down.

Clyde's routine for this level (level_hooks' second, run by player_control each frame). It reads the four cells under his feet (the engine's feet_offsets, from his screen cell $8A/$8B); with none of them water ($D0) it returns to player_control at $2C34, which ends any swimming. Already swimming ($122B set), it rejoins player_control at $2C63, past the code that would clear the special state.

Clyde has stepped into the water: $1242 set (Clyde's shots and flame stop), the special state $122B set (so the level's routines run for his jump, frames and fire), $1213 set (the panel shows the OXYGEN bar), any flame put out (flame_end), falling set ($122A), and sound effect requests $0E and $0F.
The JMP back into player_control at $2C60 that ends swim_start. The label is the engine's: level_jump_call's operand ($2D76) still held $A369, world 1's level_jump, at the hand-over.

Clyde's up and down in the water (level_hooks' third, run instead of the engine's jump and fall while $122B is set), a pixel a frame. Down held ($127D zero): see swim_sink. Up held ($127C zero) with his y at $42 or more, he rises a pixel unless one of the two cells above his head (offsets 1 and 2 in the row above, $88/$89) is solid, below first_clear; when the cell beside his head (offset 1 in his own row) is $FE, the empty sky over the pond, he jumps out instead ($1229 rising, jump step $17, the engine's rise at $2DC6). With neither held he stays at his depth.
Down held: he sinks a pixel unless one of the three cells three rows below his cell (offsets $78-$7A) is solid, below first_clear.

Clyde's frames while he swims (level_hooks' fourth). Every sixth frame ($122F from 5) the stroke $1244 steps on, 3 down to 0. His frame is the stroke's entry in swim_frames_right or swim_frames_left, by the way he faces ($122D, through swim_frame_tables into the LDA's operand at $A3F8), and the stroke's swim_bob (0, 1, 2, 1) is added to the y of both of his other sprites, the helmet and the bubbles. It ends at the engine's j_2F07, which stores the frame.
The low byte of the LDA's operand at $A3F7: $C2 for swim_frames_right, $BE for swim_frames_left (swim_frame_tables).

Run in place of player_fire while Clyde swims (level_hooks' fifth), so the fire button does nothing in the water. It calls oxygen_drain, puts the diving helmet (frame $8A) on shot sprite 1 and a bubble frame on shot sprite 2: on frames where frame_divider's $1219, $121A and $121B are all set (every eighth frame) the bubble step $1243 moves on, 3 down to 0, and picks the frame from the engine's bubble_frames ($88 $87 $86 $85). Both are white; the helmet sits 6 pixels above Clyde's y and the bubbles 8 above that; facing right the helmet is 5 pixels right of his x and the bubbles 12 left of the helmet, facing left 5 left of his x and the bubbles 15 right of it. Sprite 2 goes behind the landscape ($1218 = 4), only Clyde's own sprite stays multicolour ($1286 = 1), and the sprites' ninth x bits are cleared ($1259, $125B).
level_fire's last store ($125B) and its RTS. The label is the engine's: level_hook_call's operand ($1BA6) still held $A46B, world 1's level_fire, at the hand-over.
The bar's byte columns left with oxygen in them, 6 when full: oxygen_drain counts it down as each column empties, and a step with none left drowns Clyde.
The low bytes of the bar's six byte columns, left to right: $40A7, $40A8, $40A9 in sprite block 2 and $40E7, $40E8, $40E9 in block 3. oxygen_drain empties them from the right.

AND masks that clear one two-bit pixel of a byte: oxygen_drain uses the first four, $3F $CF $F3 $FC, last to first, so a column empties from its right-hand pixel. The other four ($C0 $30 $0C $03) and the byte after them, $18, are not read.

Called by level_fire each frame Clyde swims. When oxygen_wait runs out (every 63 frames) the bar loses a pixel: the next mask of oxygen_masks (step $1253, 3 down to 0) is ANDed into the eight rows (13-20) of the current column; when a column is empty the next one to its left starts (oxygen_column, its address from oxygen_columns into the LDA and STA). After 24 steps the bar is empty, and at the 25th, about 31 seconds of swimming from a full bar, player_hurt runs: Clyde drowns.
The low byte of the LDA's operand at $A4AE: the column being emptied (from oxygen_columns).
The operand of the AND at $A4B1: the step's mask from oxygen_masks.
The low byte of the STA's operand at $A4B3, the same column as the LDA's. Then the loop over the column's eight rows, every third byte from $15 down, and the RTS.
The full bar's eight rows, top to bottom: $55 $AA $FF $FF $AA $AA $55 $55, four two-bit pixels to the byte, so the bar shades from one sprite colour through the others and back.
